newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port strike continues over shipping bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port strike continues over shipping bill.

text.p: Many Brazilian ports faced their second day of a strike, but two of those contacted by Reuters had either returned to work Wednesday or had not stopped operations Tuesday, port officials said.
The strike is over a bill regulating inland and coastal shipping in Brazil, which is due to go to a vote in the Lower House later today.
The bill would allow foreign companies to operate shipping lines in Brazil and permit shipping companies to use their employees for tasks currently carried out by port unions.
Union leaders are talking this morning with Congressional deputies in the hope of reaching an agreement over the bill.
A plenary is then expected to take place either later tonight or tomorrow morning to decide whether to continue the strike, union officials said.
The situation in key commodity ports as of 1200 local/1400 GMT Wednesday was as follows:

* SANTOS - still on strike, 40 ships docked, 32 of which are in docks operated by CODESP port authority with the remaining eight vessels in privately-operated terminals. Of the 32 docked with CODESP, only four were operating, loading liquid chemicals. A further 27 ships are waiting to dock and 23 more are expected to arrive today. Strike costing 1.7 million reais a day.
* PARANAGUA - paralysed. 12 ships docked, three of which were loading soybeans or soyproducts. No information available on how many are waiting to dock, expected in coming days

* MACEIO - four ships docked, including two sugar vessels. One ship - the Aposteles II - is loading 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar for Syria as normal. The other, the Dodo, has stopped loading 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar, also destined for Syria. Two ships waiting to dock including one sugar vessel, the George B, which had been expected to dock today to take on 14,000 tonnes of bagged crystal sugar but which has now been delayed because of the strike

* RECIFE - has returned to work today as normal after only adhering to original proposal of 24-hour strike. Operations have resumed to load/unload 14 vessels including seven sugar ships and one wheat ship. Seven vessels waiting to dock, all of which are for general cargo

* RIO DE JANEIRO - working as normal. Has not so far participated in the strike at all. 18 ships docked including two wheat vessels (Quality of Life unloading 22,300 tonnes and the Norsul Imbituba with 12,800 tonnes wheat)

* VITORIA - Also continuing on strike. Eight vessels in the port, seven in the bay and 21 more ships expected to arrive by December 15. Of those docked, work continuing to unload one cargo of fresh fruit and another of rice from Vietnam which only had 800 tonnes left to be taken on shore. Other vessels which have ceased unloading however include cotton vessel (3,000 tonnes) and wheat ship (9,125 tonnes)
